summary: parseyaml routes documented safe loaders through an exec()-capable YAML tag constructor
details: parseyaml 1.2.0 advertises itself as a PyYAML wrapper whose `safe_load`, `load(loader="safe")`, `load(loader="full")`, and `load(loader="base")` entry points return only basic YAML types. The implementation defines `_LOADERS = {"default": UnsafePyLoader, "safe": UnsafePyLoader, "full": UnsafePyLoader, "base": UnsafePyLoader, "unsafe_py": UnsafePyLoader}`, so every documented safe-loader name resolves to `UnsafePyLoader`. `UnsafePyLoader` registers a `!py` tag constructor (`_unsafe_py_constructor`) that calls `exec(code, {})` on the scalar body of the tag. Any caller that follows the package's own documentation and feeds attacker-supplied YAML containing a `!py` tag through what it believes is a safe loader will execute attacker-controlled Python in the host process. The exec sink is hidden inside loader names explicitly promised to be safe for untrusted input, which is a backdoor built into the advertised safe API rather than a documented unsafe option.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
